header.incumbent: Homegrown billing system, built by a person who left
header.tag_why: Owen said he couldn't get it past the CFO without a number that was Pikeview's own, and the generic ROI deck was all we sent before the freeze.

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one big thing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The billing system is homegrown, built by a guy who left, and every pricing change takes them a quarter.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He wanted it done before they launched a new pricing tier, but the tier didn't have a date either.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He reached out to us.
evidence.label: fact

trigger.insight: This was a long-simmering product-and-engineering pain with no forcing event and no deadline, so nothing made the purchase urgent for anyone outside Owen's team. The key-person risk (the builder left) and the quarter-long price changes are real costs, but nobody turned them into a business case before the pitch ended.
trigger.messaging: Lead billing outreach with the cost of a homegrown system (quarter-long pricing changes, key-person risk) and give champions a way to put a dollar figure on it, instead of assuming a trigger event will show up.

evidence.excerpt: The CFO, I guess? Diane.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Owen told me. I never spoke to her.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: No. Owen said he'd bring her in at the end.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We only ever talked to product and engineering.
evidence.label: fact

decider.insight: Everything we know about the decider comes from the champion, and the rep admits she never met the CFO. The deal was single-threaded through someone who could not fund it, and the plan to bring Diane in at the end meant the person who held the budget first heard the case after it was built for someone else.
decider.messaging: Give champions a finance-ready one-pager and a CFO conversation path early, so the economic buyer is addressed in our materials and not left for the champion to translate.

evidence.excerpt: There wasn't one. It was us against doing nothing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Owen never looked at anybody else, as far as I know.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: Toward the end Owen started asking for things for finance.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "do you have something that shows payback?"
evidence.label: quote

competitor.insight: The real rival was the status quo and the CFO's funding rule, not another vendor. The change in Owen's questions, from product capability to payback, is the signal: he had started rehearsing the finance conversation and needed us to help, and that shift came about a month before the freeze.
competitor.messaging: Position against doing nothing: frame the status quo as a quantified recurring cost, since a payback question is the cue that the buyer is now fighting the budget, not a competitor.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the billing demo. Changing a price in a few clicks, trials, proration.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "that's a quarter of roadmap in five minutes."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: His engineers were into it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote

message.insight: The demo worked because it answered Owen's actual problem, engineering time lost to pricing changes. Our M7 line, 'Billing that helps you grow revenue', was explicitly rejected by the champion. The rep initially claimed nothing got silence, which hides that the audience that mattered for funding never heard any message at all.
message.messaging: Rewrite M7 around giving time back to the roadmap and removing the engineering cost of pricing changes, and keep revenue growth as a secondary point for finance.

evidence.excerpt: The freeze email.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: They missed their number in Q3 and she put a hold on all new vendor projects.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded."
evidence.label: quote

decided.insight: The freeze was the trigger, but the deal was already weak: the rep's own account shows paper sent, no signature, a month-old payback request answered with a generic deck, and a CFO who sees the project as not on fire. The rep's 'it's timing' and 'she decided against everything' explain the freeze but skip that we had a month to build the number and did not. Because the CFO's reasoning comes only through Owen, we can't say the freeze alone would have stopped a funded case.
decided.messaging: Treat a stated funding rule like 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded' as a prompt to show the cost of the status quo in the customer's own figures, rather than waiting for budget timing to improve.

evidence.excerpt: I sent him the ROI deck. The general one, with the study.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The number. Their own. What the homegrown system costs them.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: he mentioned once that some landlord subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: He also asked about migration. Moving the existing subscriptions over without asking landlords for their card details again, and whether they could do it in stages.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The gap was proof, not product: a customer-specific cost number, which M6's generic independent study could not supply. Owen had already named a cost we could have quantified (lapsed landlord subscriptions from failed cards) and we never added it up, which also happens to match our recovery capability (M10). The migration doc existed but he wanted to talk to someone who'd done it, so a reference customer was missing. Rep says nothing could have been done, which her own account contradicts.
gaps.messaging: Pair M6 with a short working session or calculator that builds the customer's own cost from their errors, engineering time and lapsed subscriptions, and add a migration reference story alongside the staged-migration doc.

evidence.excerpt: Owen's was "a tax on the roadmap."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: "I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: "if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded."
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: "we don't touch billing before renewal season."
evidence.label: quote

language.insight: The customer talks about billing as a drag on engineering and a funding rule, never as revenue growth. 'A number that's ours' is a direct rebuke of generic ROI. The renewal-season line shows a timing constraint on the engineering side too, so a freeze was not the only calendar problem. Diane's phrase is secondhand, through Owen.
language.messaging: Use 'a tax on the roadmap' and 'a number that's ours' as the framing for billing and ROI copy, in place of 'grow revenue' and 'proven ROI'.

gaps.question: Did Diane or anyone in finance actually weigh the deal, and what was her reasoning for the freeze?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen (or request a short call with Diane) what finance saw, whether Pikeview's freeze covers renewals of existing spend, and what would unfreeze it.

gaps.question: Was any other vendor or an in-house rebuild considered?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Owen whether he evaluated other billing tools or planned a rebuild; the rep only knows 'as far as I know'.

gaps.question: How far along was the deal at the freeze: procurement or just paper sent?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee what stage the paper was at, who received it, and whether legal or procurement had engaged.

gaps.question: What would a Pikeview-specific cost number have looked like, and why was the ROI session not held in the month before the freeze?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee why the session was not scheduled when Owen asked, and what inputs (errors, engineering time, lapsed landlord subscriptions) were available.

gaps.question: Did the migration questions get answered, and was a reference customer offered?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Renee whether Owen got the staged-migration doc and whether a customer who migrated billing was introduced.

close.rep_takeaway: When a champion asks for a number that is theirs, the next step is to book the session that week and ask to meet the person who funds it. A generic ROI deck plus a plan to hold that session later gave the freeze the month it needed, and 'nothing we could have done' is not supported by your own account.
